quote: Theorem 3.1 Let Xλ1, . . . , Xλn be independent nonnegative random variables with Xλi ∼ F(λi t), i = 1, . . . , n, where λi > 0, i = 1, . . . , n and F is an absolutely continuous distribution. Let r be the reverse hazard rate function of F, respectively. If t²r′(t) is increasing in t, then (λ1, . . . , λn) ≤m (θ1, . . . , θn) ⇒ Xn:n^λ ≤rh Xn:n^θ.
family: scale model Xλi ~ F(λi t) with arbitrary absolutely continuous baseline F (satisfied e.g. by generalized gamma GG(β,α), β <= 1)
compared: two parallel systems whose scale-parameter vectors are majorized
ambiguity: Stated as a recall of Khaledi et al. (2011); included as a printed theorem.

quote: Theorem 3.2 Let Xλ1, Xλ2, . . . , Xλn be independent random variables with Xλi ∼ F(λi t) where λi > 0, i = 1, . . . , n. If tr(t) is decreasing in t and t²r′(t) is increasing in t, then (λ1, . . . , λn) ≤w (θ1, . . . , θn) ⇒ Xn:n^λ ≤rh Xn:n^θ.
family: scale model; conditions hold for generalized gamma GG(β,α) with β <= 1, α > 0 (includes exponential, Weibull (β=α<=1), gamma (β=1, α<=1))
compared: parallel systems with weakly majorized scale vectors

hypotheses.text: tr(t) decreasing and t²r′(t) increasing in t
hypotheses.formal: baseline conditions (equivalently tr(t) convex and decreasing)
weak supermajorization (proof needs decreasing Schur-convex r̃)

conclusion.direction: Xn:n^λ <=rh Xn:n^θ (more dispersed scales give rh-larger maximum)

ambiguity: Glyph shows '≤w'; the Schur-convex decreasing argument identifies it as weak supermajorization.

quote: Theorem 4.1 Let Xλ1, Xλ be independent nonnegative random variables with Xλ1 ∼ F(λ1 t) and Xλ ∼ F(λt), where λ1, λ > 0 and F is an absolutely continuous distribution. Let Yλ1*, Yλ be independent nonnegative random variables with Yλ1* ∼ F(λ1*t) and Yλ ∼ F(λt), where λ1*, λ > 0. Let r be the reverse hazard rate function of F. Assume tr(t) and tr′(t)/r(t) are both decreasing in t. Suppose λ1* = min(λ, λ1, λ1*), then (λ1, λ) ≤w (λ1*, λ) ⇒ r2:2*(t)/r2:2(t) is increasing in t.
compared: ratio of reverse hazard rates of the two maxima

quote: Theorem 4.2 Let Xλ1, Xλ be independent nonnegative random variables with Xλ1 ∼ F(λ1 t) and Xλ ∼ F(λt), where λ1, λ > 0 and F is an absolutely continuous distribution. Let r be the reverse hazard rate function of F. Let Yλ1*, Yλ be independent nonnegative random variables with Yλ1* ∼ F(λ1*t) and Yλ ∼ F(λt), where λ1*, λ > 0. Assume tr(t) and tr′(t)/r(t) are both decreasing in t and t²r′(t) is increasing in t. Suppose λ1* = min(λ, λ1, λ1*), then (λ1, λ) ≤w (λ1*, λ) ⇒ X2:2 ≤lr Y2:2.
family: scale model; conditions hold for GG(β,α) with α <= β <= 1 (e.g. gamma β=1, 0<α<=1; Weibull α=β<=1)

hypotheses.text: λ1* = min(λ, λ1, λ1*) and (λ1, λ) ≼w (λ1*, λ)

quote: Corollary 4.4 Let Xλ1, Xλ2 be independent nonnegative random variables with Xλi ∼ F(λi t) for i = 1, 2. Let Y1, Y2 be independent nonnegative random variables with a common distribution Yi ∼ F(λt) for i = 1, 2. Assume tr(t) and tr′(t)/r(t) are both decreasing in t and t²r′(t) is increasing in t. Suppose λ ≤ min(λ1, λ2), then λ ≤ (λ1 + λ2)/2 ⇒ X2:2 ≤lr Y2:2.
compared: heterogeneous-scale system bounded above (in lr) by iid system with common scale λ

hypotheses.formal: common scale small enough; equivalent to (λ1,λ2) ≼w (λ,λ)

quote: Theorem 4.5 Let X1, . . . , Xn be independent nonnegative random variables such that Xi ∼ F(λ1 t) for i = 1, . . . , p and Xj ∼ F(λt) for j = p + 1, . . . , n, with λ1, λ > 0 and F is an absolutely continuous distribution. Let Y1, . . . , Yn be independent nonnegative random variables with Yi ∼ F(λ1*t) for i = 1, . . . , p and Yj ∼ F(λt) for j = p + 1, . . . , n, with λ1*, λ > 0. Let r be the reverse hazard rate function of F. Assume tr(t) and tr′(t)/r(t) are both decreasing in t. Suppose λ1* = min(λ, λ1, λ1*), then (λ1,...,λ1,λ,...,λ) ≤w (λ1*,...,λ1*,λ,...,λ) ⇒ rn:n*(t)/rn:n(t) is increasing in t.
model: parallel system, multiple-outlier model (p components at λ1/λ1*, q = n−p at λ)
compared: ratio of reverse hazard rates of the two multiple-outlier maxima

quote: Theorem 4.6 Let X1, . . . , Xn [multiple-outlier scale model as in Theorem 4.5]. ... Assume tr(t) and tr′(t)/r(t) are both decreasing in t and t²r′(t) is increasing in t. Suppose λ1* = min(λ, λ1, λ1*), then (λ1,...,λ1,λ,...,λ) ≤w (λ1*,...,λ1*,λ,...,λ) ⇒ Xn:n ≤lr Yn:n.
family: scale model; conditions hold for GG(β,α), α <= β <= 1 (subsumes Zhao–Balakrishnan Thm 3.1 for gamma 0<α<=1 when λ1* <= λ1 <= λ)
compared: maxima of two multiple-outlier systems under weak majorization

hypotheses.text: λ1* = min(λ, λ1, λ1*) and (λ1·p, λ·q) ≼w (λ1*·p, λ·q)

quote: Theorem 4.7 Let X1, . . . , Xn be independent nonnegative random variables such that Xi ∼ F(λ1 t) for i = 1, . . . , p and Xj ∼ G(λt) for j = p + 1, . . . , n, with λ1, λ > 0 and F is an absolutely continuous distribution. Let X1*, . . . , Xn* be n independent nonnegative random variables with Xi* ∼ F(λ1*t) for i = 1, . . . , p and Xj* ∼ G(λt) for j = p + 1, . . . , n, with λ1*, λ > 0. Let rF and rG be the reverse hazard rate functions of F and G, respectively. Assume trF(t) and trF′(t)/rF(t) are both decreasing in t. Suppose rF(t)/rG(t) is increasing in t, then λ1* = min(λ, λ1, λ1*) ⇒ Xn:n ≤lr Xn:n*.
model: parallel system, multiple-outlier model with two different baselines
family: scale model with baselines F (outlier group) and G (common group)
compared: systems differing in the outlier scale parameter and with different baseline pair
